akamai.coverage: plans in the public /linode/types catalog that report gpus > 0. Akamai's own pricing page lists RTX PRO 6000 plans that this API does not return, so those are missing here
akamai.name: Akamai Cloud (Linode)

datacrunch.coverage: every instance type in the public catalog that has a GPU, on-demand and spot
datacrunch.name: DataCrunch

digitalocean.coverage: every card on the public GPU Droplet pricing page, including the 12 month reserved cards, which are tagged and kept out of the on-demand tables
digitalocean.name: DigitalOcean

lambdalabs.coverage: every row of the public pricing page, all four GPU count tabs. Lambda's instance API needs a key so on-demand availability is not covered
lambdalabs.name: Lambda

runpod.coverage: every GPU type in RunPod's public catalog, on-demand and spot, but only for the markets RunPod flags as actually offering that card
runpod.name: RunPod

scaleway.coverage: GPU instance types in nine European zones. Scaleway sells other GPU products (Dedibox, managed inference) that this endpoint does not list
scaleway.name: Scaleway

anomalies: vastai RTX A2000 6GB moved from $0.1104 to $1.3356 per GPU hour (12.1x, limit 5.0x)
vastai.coverage: a fixed base list of GPU names plus whatever a six angle sample of the marketplace turns up; verified hosts only; single GPU offers preferred. A model outside both the base list and the sample does not appear
vastai.name: Vast.ai

vultr.coverage: cloud GPU (vcg) plans only, fractional and whole. Vultr bare metal GPU plans live on another endpoint and are not covered
vultr.name: Vultr
